events.title: Dutch Formosa
hints: A trading company built Fort Zeelandia on a sandbar in 1624.
It imported farm workers from the mainland and exported deerskins and sugar.
A Ming loyalist named Koxinga expelled it in 1662.
events.summary: The Dutch East India Company built Fort Zeelandia in 1624 and ran a colony on the west coast, exporting deerskins and sugar and encouraging migrants from Fujian to farm rice and sugar cane. Koxinga's forces captured the fort in 1662.

events.title: Spanish Formosa
hints: A fleet from Manila established forts in the north of the island.
Keelung and Tamsui were their bases.
The Dutch drove them out in 1642.
events.summary: Seeking a base near the China trade and to protect Manila-based shipping, Spain established forts at Keelung (San Salvador) and Tamsui in 1626. Its colony in the north was ended in 1642 when the Dutch captured Keelung.

events.title: Qing rule
hints: A dynasty from the mainland took the island after defeating the Zheng regime.
For two centuries it was a prefecture of Fujian before becoming a province in 1887.
Ceded to another empire after the 1895 treaty of Shimonoseki.
events.summary: The Qing dynasty defeated the Zheng kingdom of Tungning in 1683 and administered the island as part of Fujian until making it a separate province in 1887. Exports of sugar, rice and later tea grew, as settlement spread into aboriginal lands, until it was ceded to Japan in 1895.

events.title: French blockade and the Keelung campaign
hints: A European fleet landed troops at the northern port in 1884 during a war with the mainland.
Coal seams were one of the objectives.
The island's fishing-port archipelago to the west was also occupied in March 1885.
events.summary: During the Sino-French War, French forces captured Keelung in October 1884, seeking coal supplies and a bargaining chip, and blockaded the island. They occupied the Pescadores in March 1885 and left after the peace treaty.

events.title: Japanese rule
hints: The island was ceded to a new imperial power after a war in 1895.
It became a supplier of rice and sugar for the colonial homeland.
Rule ended with the Second World War in 1945.
events.summary: Taiwan was ceded to Japan by the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895 after the First Sino-Japanese War. Japan suppressed armed resistance, built infrastructure and developed sugar and rice production for the home market, ruling the island for fifty years until 1945.
